M/S. Sumathi Traders, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 27
July, 2020

Author: U.Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U.Durga Prasad Rao
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice U.Durga Prasad Rao
 Writ Petition No.6891 Of 2020
Order:

The petitioner prays for a writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the 3rd respondent in accepting the technical bid of the 4th respondent, who is not qualified in fulfilling the conditions of the e-procurement tender notification in Rc.No.S1/4949/2019, dated 06.02.2020 issued by the 3rd respondent calling for tender applications for supply of rice for a period of six months from 01.04.2020 to 30.09.2020, as illegal, arbitrary, discriminatory and offending Articles 14 and 19 of Constitution of India and contrary to the provisions of Andhra Pradesh Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987 and for a consequential order to set aside the notification in respect of the item of Rice and to direct to reissue fresh tender notification or alternatively ignore the tender application of 4th respondent and to pass such other order.
2. The petitioner's case is succinctly thus.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: ( a) The petitioner is a Proprietary concern at Tirupati dealing in commodities like Rice, Sugar, Ghee etc., and also the Milk products.

He used to participate in tenders for supply of above items for preparation of Prasadams,
Annadanam etc., conducted by the religious institutions and has rich experience in that field.
Besides, the petitioner is holder of various State Licences like GST Licence, FSSAI and Agmark Licences.
He also obtained licence bearing UDPR, J No.10114010000306 under The A.P. Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, dated 11.02.2015.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: (b) While so, the 3rd respondent issued an e-procurement tender notification vide its proceedings Rc.No.S1/4949/2019, dated 06.02.2020 published in Eenadu Telugu Daily on 07.02.2020 inviting separate tender applications for supply of Rice and other items and made available the tender forms on its website.
As per the notification, the tender process is under two stages.

The 'technical bid'
relating to the qualifications of a tenderer, will be opened on 25.02.2020 and 'financial bid' or 'price bid' will be opened on 27.02.2020.
The tender conditions in respect of items of procurement are same.
As per the tender conditions, the tenderer should satisfy the eligibility criteria consisting of several requirements.
The tenderer should upload 15 documents to qualify for the technical bid.
Unless such mandatory eligibility criteria is satisfied, no tenderer will be eligible to be qualified in the technical bid and he will not be considered for price bid.

The eligibility criteria/qualifications M/S. Sumathi Traders, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 27 July, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100168575/
1 will be strictly scrutinized with reference to the supporting documents during the stage of technical bid.

sentences.text: For instance, if a tenderer is not holding GST registration, Dealers Licence, FSSAI and Agmark Licences or any other certificate/licence against the relevant item noted in the tender form, his tender application will be rejected.
(c) The petitioner holds all the licences as mentioned in the notification under the caption of 'upload documents' which are UDPR, J mandatory.
His documents were scrutinized for technical bid and they were accepted which is a matter of record.

However the 4th respondent is concerned, he was not holding the required licence/certificates as mentioned at,
a) Item No.7 i.e., Experience Certificate,
b) Item No.10 i.e., Annual Turnover Certificate,
c) Item No.12 i.e., Evidences for supply of relevant material for the last three years made to State Government/Semi Government Sectors,
d) Item No.13 i.e., Certificate of Quality Test and e) Item No.14 i.e., Agmark Licence (which was expired by March,2019).
(d) For satisfying the requirement under Item Nos.7 and 10, the 4th respondent has produced self-handwritten statement which cannot be treated as Experience Certificate and Turnover Certificate issued by competent authority.
He also failed to produce certificate of Quality Test obtained from Government Recognized Certifying Agency for the items of tenders except for Bengal Gram.
Thus, the 4th respondent has not fulfilled the vital requirements.

(e) In order to maintain transparency and prevent irregularities and secure quality services to the pilgrims, the 2nd respondent issued Circular No.B1/37487/2013 dated 10.03.2016 making certain conditions mandatory which covers the irregularities pointed out supra.
The 2nd respondent has indicated that the deviations if any would be viewed seriously and disciplinary action would be initiated UDPR, J against the concerned.

Added to it, the rules issued in G.O.Ms.No.866 Revenue (Endowments-I) Department, dated 08.08.2003 also mandate that the issuance of all leases or licenses by way of public auction shall maintain transparency, competitive bid and quality services.
In the instant case, the technical bid deals with the eligibility criteria which has taken care of safety of pilgrims also.
Therefore, the production of certain licences from various governmental departments was made mandatory.

However, the Executive Officer of 3rd respondent has ignored all the tender conditions, Circulars of the 2nd respondent and relevant rules and took a decision to allow 4th respondent to compete for price bid and therefore the action of the 3rd respondent in accepting the bid of 4th respondent in respect of the item of rice is bad in law, being illegal,
arbitrary, discriminatory and offending Articles 14 and 19 of the Constitution of India and Contrary to the Provisions of Andhra Pradesh Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987.

sentences.text: Hence, the writ petition.
3. The 3rd respondent filed counter inter alia contending thus.

The petitioner's family is having two agencies namely (1) M/s. Sumathi Traders and (2) M/s Sri Vinayaka Agencies and participating in the 3rd respondent's tender process since long time, year by year.

Since last UDPR, J several years,
no third agency is coming forward to participate in the tender process.
Presently, M/s Vinayaka Agency is supplying all the items required and the said agency got qualified in pursuance of the tender notification issued last year for a period of one year.
This year, the duration of supply of items is reduced to six months as per the Circular dated 25.05.2019 issued by the 2nd respondent in the interest of Endowment Institution.

Earlier, for supply of all items, only one tender notification used to be issued but at present the single tender was divided into nine tenders such as rice, sugar,
cashew nut, Cardamoms and Bengal Gram dal powder, Cow ghee, Raisins, Toor dal and other provisions in order to facilitate all the prospective bidders to participate in the auction and the 3rd respondent to get a lower price.
The present writ petition is filed to stall the supply by the third agency and to continue M/s Sri Vinayaka Agency.
(a) The 4th respondent is concerned, the said agency is directly supplying the rice without any middleman.
The main aim and objective of the tender is to allow as many participants and to supply rice at a competitive price in order to reduce the expenditure towards purchase of rice.
Therefore, all the bidders were made to qualify in the technical bid process.

In the price bid, whoever quoted less price, they were awarded tender for that item only by virtue of the initiation taken by the 3rd respondent and in that process an amount of Rs.10 lakhs for a period of six months was saved comparing to the last year tender price.

The 4th respondent has quoted Rs.38.99 per 1 Kg UDPR, J whereas the petitioner quoted 45.99 per 1 Kg of rice, and when it comes to M/s Sri Vinayaka Agency it is now supplying the rice at Rs.46.25 per 1 Kg.

Even though they quoted highest price, the petitioner approached the court to see that the tender process is stalled and as a result the present supplying agency should continue the supply of rice beyond the period of 01.04.2020.

(b) The 3rd respondent further contended that as per the tender Condition No.43, the Executive Officer reserves rights to terminate/amend/modify the contract without assigning any reason or advance notice to the tenderer/supplier and similarly, the terms of the tender may be amended/modified by the Executive Officer, if necessary to ensure competitiveness and quality of procurement.
Therefore, the tender was awarded as per the rules and powers vested with the 3rd respondent in the interest of the institution.

So far as the Circular dated 10.03.2016 is concerned,
the same was modified by another Circular dated 25.03.2019 which deals with all issues regarding the tender process.
Therefore, the 3rd respondent has not violated any conditions in the Circular dated 10.03.2016.

(c) In order to reduce the expenditure on purchase of rice and to utilize the saved amount for the basic amenities of the devotees, the 3rd respondent has taken a decision to allow all the participants in the technical bid and price bid.
Hence, there is no illegality in awarding tender to the bidders who quote less price.

It is submitted that as per the tender conditions, the petitioner's Agmark Licence is going to UDPR, J expire on 31.03.2020 but in spite of the same, the petitioner's bid was considered in the technical evaluation as well as in the price bid.

The petitioner also not complied with the M/S. Sumathi Traders, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 27 July, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100168575/
3 mandatory condition i.e., to submit the hard copies with attestation.

sentences.text: Without attestation, the petitioner has submitted the all hard copies but in spite of the same he was allowed to participate in the tender process i.e., technical bid.
The 3rd respondent is filing a comparative table of price pertaining to previous tender rate and present rate to show how it saved Rs.10 lakhs for a period of six months.

Further, before taking stock of the items from the bidders, the 3rd respondent takes every necessary care and after satisfying with the quality only payments will be made to the bidders and no advance payments would be made to any bidders in this regard.
Thus, the writ petition may be dismissed.

4. Heard learned counsel for petitioner, Sri V. Venugopala Rao, learned Government Pleader for Endowments representing respondent Nos.1 and 2, Sri G. Ramana Rao, learned Standing Counsel for respondent No.3 and Sri M. Venkata Ramana, learned counsel for respondent No.4.
5.

The main plank of argument of Sri V. Venugopala Rao, learned counsel for petitioner is that supply of rice for the preparation of Prasadams and Annadanam in the holy shrine of 3rd respondent deity is considered more as a sacred duty and pious obligation rather than mere discharging of a commercial contract.

Whoever succeeds in the bid must be able to cope up with the demand for rice made by the UDPR, J 3rd respondent authority and should supply the quality rice within the prescribed time periodically during the currency of the contract.
Any slight deviation would adversely effect the preparation of daily Prasadams and Annadanam at the temple and also severely hurt the religious sentiments of the devotees.

He would vehemently argue that in view of the fact that the 3rd respondent temple is one of the famous temples in the state of Andhra Pradesh and large number of devotees visit to offer prayers and treat that having Prasadams and Annadanams at the temple as fulfilment of sacred deed, the 3rd respondent has rightly incorporated stern conditions and rigorous qualifications for a bidder.

6. In further expatiation, learned counsel would submit that an intending bidder in order to qualify himself in the technical bid, must have an annual turnover of Rs.One Crore, besides having experience in supply of rice in the past three years to State Government/Semi Government sectors/Central Government institutions.

That apart, he must possess several certificates and licences like Registration of Firm; GST registration; Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Commodities Dealer's Licence; Copy of valid FSSAI (Food Safety and Standards Authority of India); Income Tax Returns for the past three years; Experience Certificate of the supply of the relevant commodities of bulk quantities for the last three years; copy of Agmark Licence etc.

sentences.text: Besides, the tenderer must deposit an EMD amount of Rs.6,00,000/-.

Learned counsel would argue that it is only after the tenderer submits UDPR, J all the aforesaid documents and fulfils the qualification criteria, his technical bid will be validated and considered for financial bid/price bid.
He would emphasise that without passing the technical bid, one cannot qualify for financial bid.
That is why two different dates i.e., 25.02.2020 and 27.02.2020 are set apart for opening of technical bid and price bid respectively.
Learned counsel would further argue that the 4th respondent in whose favour bid was knocked down, has miserably failed to fulfil several crucial qualification tests concerning to technical bid.

For instance, the 4th respondent did not hold Experience Certificate; Annual Turnover Certificate; Evidences for supply of relevant material to the State Government/Semi Government sectors for the last three years; Certificate of Quality Test and Agmark licence as M/S. 4 mentioned in the tender notification.

sentences.text: Instead of submitting the Experience Certificate issued by the concerned organizations, the 4th respondent has produced a self-handwritten statement which is not valid.
In spite of the above severe shortcomings in the technical bid offered by the 4th respondent, the 3rd respondent approved his bid on the sole ground that he offered less price of Rs.38.99 per 1 Kg.
Learned counsel reiterated that the financial bid of a tenderer will be relevant only when his technical bid is approved.

Since he failed in the preliminary stage itself, the question of considering his financial bid does not arise and hence the action of the 3rd respondent is a clear infraction of Articles 14 and 19 of the Constitution.

He hypothetically argued that had the technical UDPR, J qualifications were not mentioned as they were excepted in the case of 4th respondent,
many more bidders would have participated and quoted far lesser price than offered by the 4th respondent.

He thus argued that the entire tender process is vitiated and therefore the same may be set aside.
7.

Per contra, while opposing the writ petition Sri G. Ramana - Rao, learned Standing Counsel for 3rd respondent argued that the petitioner's family is having two agencies viz., M/s. Sumathi Traders and M/s.Vinayaka Agency and since long they have been regularly participating in tender process and supplying all the items to 3rd respondent and thereby no third agency is coming forward.
Therefore, to give a fair opportunity to all tenderers on competitive bid basis and thereby to save valuable amount donated by the devotees, the 3rd respondent took measures.
As a part of it, he submitted, the duration of supply is reduced from one year to six months i.e., from 01.04.2020 to 30.09.2020.
Further, the tenderers are instructed to submit separate tenders for each item instead of a single tender which was in vogue previously.
Further, in order to invite the competitive bid at the lowest price, the bid of the 4th respondent was accepted though he did not fulfil certain qualifications.
Learned Standing Counsel argued that the 4th respondent agency is directly supplying the rice without the intervention of the middleman.
In that view, he offered a lowest price at Rs.38.99 per Kg as against the petitioner's bid of Rs.45.99 per Kg and M/s.
Sri Vinayaka Agency's UDPR, J bid of Rs.46.25 per Kg.

Learned counsel would submit that the bid of 4th respondent was accepted as it being the lowest one and thereby the 3rd respondent could save Rs.10 Lakhs over a period of six months in compassion to the previous year's tender price.
Learned counsel sought to defend the action of 3rd respondent on the strength of Condition No.43 of tender conditions.
Referring to it, learned counsel vehemently argued that the 3rd respondent has reserved right to amend/modify the terms of the tender to ensure competitiveness and quality of the procurement.
In that view, the 3rd respondent accepted the technical bid of all the participants and ultimately accepted the price bid of 4th respondent since his being the lowest.

He emphatically argued that since the petitioner has not challenged the validity of Condition No.43 he cannot now question the action of 3rd respondent in accepting the technical bid of all the participants and finally accepting the price bid of the 4th respondent.

Learned counsel pointed out that infact the Agmark licence of the petitioner is going to expire on 31.03.2020 and it is not known whether he can secure the said licence during the currency of contract i.e., from 01.04.2020 to 30.09.2020.
Therefore, it can be said that the technical bid of the petitioner is also defective one and it could be rejected.
However, to give a fair chance, the 3rd respondent accepted the technical bid of all the participants including the petitinoer's.
He thus, prayed to dismiss the writ petition.

9. The point for consideration is whether there are merits in the writ petition to allow?
10. POINT:
The admitted facts are that the 3rd respondent has floated e-tender for procurement of rice for preparation of Prasadams and Naivedyam for the period from 01.04.2020 to 30.09.2020.
The tender process is under two stages.
The first stage relates to technical bid and second one relates to price bid and both bids are notified to be opened separately on 25.02.2020 and 27.02.2020 respectively.

The important conditions for fulfilling technical bid are:
a) Offering EMD amount of Rs.Six Lakhs.
b) GST registration c) A.P. Scheduled Commodities Dealers Licence in force. Copy of Valid food Grain Licence.

i) Letter towards authorized signatory to sign and submit bid in the case of dealers not attended etc.
j) Annual Turnover certificate of Food Grains of Rs.1 Crore in the year 2016-17,

The supplier should have supplied atleast Rice metric tons last Financial year 2018-19.
The supplier should produce evidence in supply to State Govt/Semi Govt sectors.
m) Certificate of Quality test from a Government Recognized certifying Agency.
n) Copy of Agmark Licence.
o) A firm participating in the bidding should atleast have its branch office located in Rayalaseema Zone of Andhra Pradesh at Chittoor (or) Tirupathi for operational convenience.

sentences.text: UDPR, J 13.
On a close scrutiny of Condition No.43, this Court agrees with the argument of 3rd respondent.
Condition No.43 reads thus.
"The SSVVSD, reserves the right to terminate/amend/modify the contract without assigning any reason or advance notice to the tenderer/Supplier.

Similarly, the terms of the tender may be amended/modified by SSVVSD, If necessary, to ensure competitiveness and quality of procurement."
14.
As can be seen, Condition No.43 is in two parts.
First part reads as "The SSVVSD, reserves the right to terminate/amend/modify the contract without assigning any reason or advance notice to the tenderer/Supplier".
By this condition, the Devasthanam reserves the right to terminate/amend/modify the contract without assigning any reason or advance notice to the tenderer/supplier.
This right relates to terminating or cancelling or modifying the contract without assigning reasons and without giving advance notice to the tenderer/supplier.
This right arises only after the parties entered into the contract.
More vividly, the right to terminate/amend or modify the contract arises only after the contract came into existence.

Since the present case has not reached to that stage, it is wholly unnecessary to discuss and resolve whether the 3rd respondent can reserve its right to terminate, amend and modify the contract without assigning any reason and without giving any advance notice to the other party.

15. Then, the 2nd para of Condition No.43 reads as if the Devasthanam reserves the right to amend,
modify the terms of the tender to ensure competitiveness and quality of procurement.
The UDPR, J second part relates to the stage of tender process and it gives a right to 3rd respondent to amend or modify the terms of the tender.
As rightly argued by the learned Standing Counsel for 3rd respondent, this condition is not challenged by the petitioner.
Therefore, under the second part of Condition No.43, the 3rd respondent can amend or modify the terms of the tender.
Exercising this power, it appears, the 3rd respondent has waived the rigour of the qualifications relating to technical bid and qualified all the tenderers.

Had he qualified only one of the disqualified tenderers,
that might amount to violation of Article 14 of Constitution of India.
However, he qualified all the tenderers.
As rightly argued by learned counsel for 3rd respondent, though the petitioner had possessed Agmark licence up to 31.03.2020 only but not beyond that, still his technical bid was also approved.
However, since the bid of the 4th respondent was the lowest one, the same was accepted by the 3rd respondent.
In the entire process, the 3rd respondent cannot be found fault for not following fair procedure or giving equal opportunity.
Therefore, I see no merits in the case of the petitioner.
16. Accordingly, this writ petition is dismissed.
No costs.
As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
